purpose: The machine-readable form of this repository's quality policy. It says which verification exists, what each level of evidence proves, and which gate a change has to pass. The prose version is docs/development.md; the taxonomy itself is in CLAUDE.md.

stack.package_manager_deviation: The project-init house rule names Bun for JavaScript/TypeScript. This project ships to npm with package-lock.json as its lockfile and CI installs with `npm ci`; switching the package manager would change the published reproducibility mechanism, so npm stays.

verification_taxonomy.example: src/api/index.ts exists and `mise run typecheck` passes.

verification_taxonomy.meaning: Covered by a green test in CI.
verification_taxonomy.example: test/api.test.ts drives the public API against the in-repo fake host.

verification_taxonomy.meaning: Verified against the in-repo fake AE host, not against a real After Effects.
verification_taxonomy.example: Every test under test/ runs host/a8n-host.js verbatim against src/testing/fake-ae/.

verification_taxonomy.meaning: Observed running against an installed After Effects.

change_to_verification.change: Documentation only, no code or host script
change_to_verification.notes: docs/verification.md JSX snippets are still ES3-checked; that is part of the fast gate.
The host script ships verbatim and must stay ES3. `node --check` plus the ES3 test cover syntax; the release gate adds the packaging checks.

change_to_verification.change: Public API surface, package exports, or the published shape
change_to_verification.notes: scripts/check-public-api.js and scripts/check-packed-package.js are the gate that a broken `exports` map cannot survive.

change_to_verification.change: Anything that must be proven against a real After Effects
change_to_verification.notes: Integration is manual and opt-in; it is recorded in docs/verification.md, never asserted from a fake-host run.

change_to_verification.change: Version bump, publish, or release tooling
change_to_verification.notes: docs/releasing.md holds the procedure; publishing itself needs a human approval with 2FA.

canonical_entry_points.integration: Manual, opt-in, against an installed After Effects. The procedure and the recorded results are docs/verification.md. There is no automated integration runner; a skipped or absent integration run is reported as `fake/mock only` or `not verified`, never as `verified on real host`.

integration.notes: Opt-in. Absent an After Effects install there is nothing to run and nothing to claim.

release.scope: the quality gate, the build, the ES3 host check, the documented-snippet check, and the packed-package and public-API checks

check.covers: typecheck, lint, test, build, ES3 host parse, documented JSX snippets, packed package, public API

release-tooling-windows.covers: the release tooling's tests on native Windows with CRLF checkouts

ci.cost_policy: The fast PR gate is one job; the Windows release-tooling job is the only platform-specific cost and it runs on every PR because it covers a checkout shape (CRLF) the unit suite does not reproduce.

coverage_policy.notes: There is no coverage tool in the dependency set and no threshold. Coverage is therefore not a gate, and a passing suite says nothing about how much of the bridge was exercised. Do not read a green suite as coverage.

macos.notes: After Effects 2026 (26.5x89), macOS 27, arm64. See docs/verification.md.

windows.notes: The launcher path exists and the release tooling is tested there, but no After Effects behaviour has been observed on Windows. No behaviour is claimed.

false_green: A test that skips, is `.only`, or asserts nothing.
A command with `|| true`, a no-fail flag, or a blanket ignore.
A green result reported against a predecessor's SHA rather than the current one.
A fake-host run presented as `verified on real host`.
A manual check that happened but was not recorded in docs/verification.md.
A lowered threshold or a disabled CI check.
recompile_triggers: A framework, runtime, or toolchain major version changes.
The public API or the package `exports` map changes shape.
A CI workflow changes its jobs, runners, or required checks.
A new platform target is claimed.
A regression escapes and the gate that should have caught it did not.
The release model (branch topology, publish path) changes.
